title: Permission inventory crawler: enumerate API routes + seed sensitivity annotations
creator: Kaitlyn Nguyen
description:
Goal: build a repeatable crawler/script that enumerates Redwood control-plane + console backend API routes and outputs seed rows for the RBAC v2 permission inventory sheet.

This is intended to reduce manual inventory effort and establish a durable mechanism for ongoing governance (new endpoint => must be represented in inventory + permission taxonomy).

Outputs:
- A generated CSV/JSON file containing route metadata (service, method, path, handler, authn required, current RBAC v1/v2 check presence when detectable) and placeholders for sensitivity + proposed RBAC v2 action.
- A "delta" mode that flags newly-added/removed routes since last run.

Non-goals (for this ticket):
- Perfect semantic sensitivity classification (we still need human review per the rubric).
- Deep runtime/data-plane inference authorization (explicitly out of scope for initial inventory).

References:
- Permission inventory methodology (Confluence): sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/permission-inventory-methodology.json
- RBAC v2 overview: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/rbac-v2-overview.json
- Eng standard: authz check standard: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/authz-check-standard.json

Acceptance criteria:
1) Script can enumerate routes from:
   - Control plane (Go) HTTP router
   - Console backend (TS) routes
   - API gateway route registry (where applicable) OR at minimum reads consolidated OpenAPI/service spec.
2) For each route, output includes:
   - service_name
   - owning_team (if available; otherwise blank)
   - http_method
   - path_template
   - source (control-plane | console | gateway | other)
   - handler identifier (file:line or function name best-effort)
   - authn_required (best-effort)
   - current_authz_enforcement: missing | partial | ok | unknown (best-effort)
   - suggested_resource (blank unless confidently inferred)
   - suggested_action (blank unless confidently inferred)
   - sensitivity (blank; to be filled via review)
   - notes (freeform)
3) Delta mode: compares prior output and prints a summary + emits a "new_routes.csv" for review.
4) Deterministic output ordering and stable IDs (service + method + path) to reduce sheet churn.
5) Documented run instructions and where output is checked in / uploaded.

Implementation notes / approach:
- Control plane: use the compiled route table that the server registers at startup (we already use this for some metrics tagging). Add a debug endpoint or a build-time extract?
  - Preferred: add a small package exposing route metadata (method, template, handler name) so the script can import it and dump JSON without running the server.
- Console backend: use the central router definition (Express/Router) and require() it in a node script to list registered routes (or parse a route manifest if we have one).
- Authn/authz inference heuristics:
  - authn_required: detect presence of standard auth middleware (e.g., RequireSession/RequireAPIKey/RequireOrgScopedActor) at route registration.
  - current_authz_enforcement: attempt to detect calls to the new authz middleware wrapper (RBAC v2) OR legacy RBAC v1 checks.
  - If detection is ambiguous, mark unknown and rely on manual audit.
- Output format:
  - Primary: CSV (easy import to Google Sheet)
  - Secondary: JSONL for tooling/automation.

Risks:
- Heuristics may produce false negatives for authz checks (e.g., checks performed deeper in handlers). Mitigation: label as "unknown" rather than "missing" unless we’re confident.
- Route parsing for TS may be brittle if routes are dynamically composed. Mitigation: prefer a manifest approach if available.

Deliverables / where to land:
- Repo: redwood/control-plane (tools/permission_inventory/)
- Repo: redwood/console-backend (tools/permission_inventory/)
- Output artifacts stored in a versioned directory (e.g., artifacts/permission_inventory/YYYY-MM-DD/*.csv) and attached to the permission inventory sheet workflow.

Follow-ups:
- Wire into CI as a non-blocking job to produce route deltas per PR (ties into governance work / later conformance enforcement).
- Extend to include private admin surfaces once the private installer/admin API route inventory is stable.
comments: 2025-02-05 (Benji Okafor): Spike: control-plane routes are registered via chi router with a central mount table. We can collect method+pattern+handler by wrapping the route registration helpers. Need to confirm handler name extraction in prod builds (inlining can lose names).

2025-02-06 (Amara Diallo): Gateway has a route registry but it’s not canonical for all internal admin endpoints. Please don’t over-index on gateway; control-plane and console backend should be the source of truth for the inventory seed.

2025-02-07 (Brian Murphy): Recommend stable route IDs: `${service}:${method}:${path}`. Also add a field for "visibility" (public vs internal) if you can infer from router group prefixes (/admin, /internal).

2025-02-10 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): For "current_authz_enforcement", be conservative. If you can’t prove a check exists, set unknown (not missing). The inventory sheet will drive explicit manual review anyway.

2025-02-12 (Benji Okafor): Implemented control-plane extractor as a go test that imports the router and serializes a route manifest. This avoids starting the server. Output: JSON + CSV. Handler identifiers are file:line when available via runtime.Caller in the wrapper.

2025-02-14 (Chloe Martin): Console backend routes aren’t easily enumerable from Express once composed; but we do have a central "routeDefs" list used for OpenAPI generation. Use that rather than parsing express internals.

2025-02-17 (Benji Okafor): Added delta mode: compares current manifest to a prior snapshot and prints counts (added/removed/changed). 'changed' is method/path/service differences only; notes/sensitivity aren’t part of diff.

2025-02-18 (Marcus Lin): Please ensure output includes a column for 'actor_types' (user, api_key, support_impersonation, break_glass) even if blank. Inventory methodology expects it. OK for now to leave blank; we’ll fill during review.
updates: 2025-02-19: Marked In Review. Control-plane + console backend extractors implemented. Need final review on output columns (actor_types addition) and docs/runbook for Security Eng to use weekly during inventory phase.
